title: Percent as a rate per 100
summary: Partners use a hundred grid and a tape diagram to find a percent of a quantity and the whole from a part (6.RP.A.3c), explaining each step in words before writing numbers.

standard.text: Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems, e.g., by reasoning about tables of equivalent ratios, tape diagrams, double number line diagrams, or equations.

discourse: Explain a percent as a rate per 100 and connect it to a model: 30% means 30 out of every 100 squares, or 30 hundredths of the tape.
Walk a listener through a percent calculation in order, naming what each number in the model stands for (the whole, the part, the percent).
Tell apart what was taken away and what remains in a discount story, and say which one the question asks for.
sentence: Percent statements where of signals multiplication: 25% of 40 dollars is 10 dollars.
Part-whole sentences with is and of in fixed places: ___ is ___% of ___ (12 is 20% of what number?).
Noun groups from shopping: 25% off, a 25% discount, the sale price, the original price.
word: Percent read as per cent, per hundred; the root cent- (hundred) also appears in century, centimeter and Spanish centavo and ciento.
The near-homophones of and off: of means multiply by the percent; off means subtract the discount from the original price.
Benchmark percents spoken as fractions: 50% is half, 25% is one fourth, 10% is one tenth.

contentObjective: Students will find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100 and find the whole when given a part and the percent, using hundred grids and tape diagrams (6.RP.A.3c).
languageObjective: Students will explain percent calculations step by step using ___% of ___ is ___ and sequence words, naming the whole, the part and the percent in their model.

L1-2: ___ out of 100 squares are shaded. That is ___%.
The whole is ___. The part is ___. (Word bank: whole, part, percent, of, off)
L3-4: First, I found 10% of ___, which is ___. Then I ___.
___ is ___% of ___, because each 10% of the tape stands for ___.
The jacket is ___% off, so I subtract ___ from the original price.
L5-6: Since ___% means ___ per 100, I can scale the ratio ___ : 100 to ___ : ___.
The question asks for the ___, not the ___, so after finding ___ I still need to ___.
Another way to check is to use the benchmark ___%, which tells me ___.

vocabulary.definition: a rate per 100; 30% means 30 out of every 100
vocabulary.morphology: per 'for each' + cent 'hundred'; Spanish por ciento has the same parts

vocabulary.definition: a piece of the whole; in a percent problem, the amount that matches the percent
the full amount that stands for 100%
vocabulary.morphology: sounds like hole; spelling with w- signals the math meaning

vocabulary.definition: an amount taken off the original price
vocabulary.morphology: dis- 'away' + count; Spanish des- matches English dis-

vocabulary.definition: a familiar value used to estimate or check, such as 50% for half
vocabulary.morphology: compound: bench + mark, first a surveyor's reference mark

vocabulary.definition: a rectangle split into equal sections to show parts of a whole
vocabulary.morphology: diagram and diagrama are cognates; tape and cinta are not

vocabulary.definition: two number lines that line up equivalent amounts, such as percents above and quantities below
vocabulary.morphology: double and doble are cognates; line and recta are not

vocabulary.definition: one of 100 equal parts of a whole
vocabulary.morphology: hundred + -th (ordinal); Spanish centésima uses the cent- root instead

activity.title: Hundred-Grid Sale Talk
steps: Give each pair a 10-by-10 grid and a blank tape divided into 10 equal sections. Write 100% under the end of the tape and $40 above it.
Partner A shades 25 squares and says, 25 out of 100, so 25%. Partner B labels the tape: each section is 10% and stands for $4.
Together, partners solve the jacket problems below. One partner explains each step aloud with First / Then / So; the other writes only after hearing the explanation.
Swap roles for the class survey problem and the find-the-whole problem. The writer must name the whole, the part and the percent in the margin before writing an answer.
Quick check: hold up of or off cards while you read three short sale phrases; partners explain one choice to the class.

problems.prompt: A jacket costs $40 and is 25% off. How many dollars do you save?
What is the sale price of the jacket?
In a class of 30 students, 60% walk to school. How many students walk?
Twelve students chose soccer. That is 20% of the grade. How many students are in the grade?

warmup: Write cent on the board and ask partners for every word they know with cent in it, in any language (century, centimeter, centavo, ciento, cien). Agree that cent means hundred. Then read aloud: 50 percent, 10 percent, 100 percent; partners say each one as ___ out of 100 and as a fraction (half, one tenth, the whole).
